President Trump campaigns today in South Carolina
to give a boost to Senator Darlene Graham.
She's running for the seat previously held by her late brother Lindsey Graham.
Last night, Trump was in North Carolina and appears Tamara Keith reports the president
made an unusual observation about the Senate race in that state.
Trump was there to campaign for his hand-picked Republican Senate nominee Michael Watley.
Polls show him trailing North Carolina's former governor Roy Cooper, a Democrat.
And Republican groups have essentially abandoned Watley on the air.
Moving their money to more competitive states.
In the midst of criticizing Cooper, Trump seemed to concede that the Democrat is going to win.
And he's going to become your senator and it's crazy.
It was a throwaway line, but one that appeared to reflect the political reality on the ground.
Trump called on his supporters to vote as if he's on the ballot.
Tamara Keith, NPR News, Greenville, North Carolina.
Russian President Vladimir Putin says he has freed American Stephen Hubbard from a Russian
prison following a request from President Trump.
Hubbard had been sentenced to nearly seven years behind bars.
The announcement came on the same day as talks between Putin and White House envoy Steve
Whitkoff.
Their focus on U.S. efforts and Russia's war against Ukraine.
More from NPR's Charles Mains.
74-year-old Stephen Hubbard of Michigan was detained by Russian forces in Ukraine in 2022
and later sentenced for serving as a mercenary in the Ukrainian army.
He's now a free man.
Speaking before cameras, as talks with White House envoy Steve Whitkoff got underway in
Russia's former imperial capital of St. Petersburg, President Putin announced Hubbard had been
released and was already at the airport.
Earlier this week, President Trump said he'd asked Putin to release Hubbard, whom the U.S.
had formally designated "wrongfully detained."
Hubbard's release comes as Trump has lifted some sanctions on Moscow and openly criticized
Ukraine amid U.S. efforts to negotiate an end to the war.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
Israel's security forces detained a group of activists, including an American running
for Congress, Brad Lander, who has since been released.
They were helping Palestinians harvest olives during a surge of attacks by Israeli settlers
in the occupied West Bank.
More from NPR's Ruth Sherlock.
Among this group of activists, about 80 people, there were American rabbis from the group
Truer, many whom had flown from the U.S. for this, and the Israeli group, Rabbis for Human
Rights.
So they really hoped that they could dissuade attacks from settlers or from the army preventing
them to picking their olives.
The group did manage to pick olives for about two hours, but then we started hearing drones
overhead, and the Israeli military and police arrived and declared the area a closed military
zone.
Israeli lawyers say this was the largest mass detention of activists in the occupied West
Bank in at least 10 years.
This is NPR News.
The Supreme Court is blocking the Trump administration from immediately enforcing new medical restrictions
for transgender people in prison.
Today's decision leaves in place a lower court ruling that prevented the policy from taking
effect.
CNN is threatening new legal action if the Trump administration continues to deny its
journalists access to Air Force One and the pool of journalists who accompany Trump when
he travels.
Last week, a federal judge had granted CNN, MS Now and Politico their request for a preliminary
injunction against the administration's ban while the dispute continues to be litigated.
Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, has approved what supporters are calling one of the most
generous paid parental leave policies in the country.
Julia Zenkovich with Member Station WESA says the county includes Pittsburgh.
Under the plan, most employers in Allegheny County must provide parents 12 weeks of fully
paid leave following the birth or adoption of a child or a stillbirth.
In an 11-4 vote, the county council approved the measure, with supporters citing the broad
public health benefits.
Shortly before the vote, Council Democrat Dan Grisbick said that other counties would likely
be watching the outcome of Tuesday's vote.
"We've waited decades for Washington and Harrisburg to act, and tonight Allegheny County can be
the first county in the nation to stop waiting and start doing."
Chief Executive Sarah Inamorado, a progressive Democrat who championed the policy, plans
to sign it into law.
For NPR News, I'm Julia Zenkovich in Pittsburgh.
U.S. stocks trading higher with the NASDAQ up 288 points are more than 1 percent.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
